samples.summary: undo/redo clear `selectedImage` but leave `imageResizeDrag` live, so an in-flight resize can commit onto the wrong (or vanished) inline
samples.evidence: `undoFn` (line 2104) and `redoFn` (line 2139) now set `selectedImage = null` but do not touch `imageResizeDrag`, while `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (3913-3914) and `dispose` (3931-3932) clear both. A resize drag is armed at 2603-2615 from `selectedImage` and keeps its own `blockId`/`offset`. Undo is reachable while the mouse is still down: the keyboard ⌘Z reaches `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all (2442), which nulls `selectedImage`, returns false, and TextEditor invokes `undoFn` (wired at 2263). After the undo the drag state survives: `render()` takes the `if (imageResizeDrag)` branch at 1845 and paints a preview overlay for a selection that no longer exists, and on mouseup `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (2515) writes `applyInlineStyle` at the stale `(blockId, offset)` — which after the undo shifted offsets can name a *different* image, silently resizing the wrong one. The same reasoning the diff uses to justify clearing the selection applies to the drag that is measured in the same coordinate.

samples.summary: `handleImageResizeMouseUp` still uses throwing `getBlock` with a dead `block ?` guard — the one stale-coordinate reader the delta did not harden
samples.evidence: Line 2538: `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId); const current = block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null;`. `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187), so the `block ?` ternary can never see a falsy value and the intended guard is dead — the throw escapes the document-level `mouseup` listener. This is exactly the hazard the delta fixed in `selectImageAt`, `getSelectedImage` and `updateSelectedImage` by switching to `findBlock`; this sibling path, which holds the same kind of stale `(blockId, offset)` coordinate across an arbitrarily long drag (during which a remote peer edit, or an undo per the finding above, can remove the block), was left on `getBlock`.

samples.summary: `resetAfterDocumentReplace` nulls `imageResizeDrag` without unregistering the drag listeners or resetting the canvas cursor
samples.evidence: Line 3914 sets `imageResizeDrag = null`, but the `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners added at 2614-2615 and the `canvas.style.cursor = cursorForHandle(handle)` set at 2613 are only undone inside `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (2522-2525), which now returns immediately at its `if (!imageResizeDrag) return;` guard (2516). If the document is replaced while a drag is in flight, the resize cursor stays stuck on the canvas and the two document listeners remain attached until `dispose()`. Compare `handleImageResizeMouseUp`, which deliberately tears both down before nulling the drag.

samples.summary: `splitTableCell` (and `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn`) clear the image selection even when the underlying doc op is a no-op
samples.evidence: The clears are placed after the `if (!cellInfo) return` guard only, so `splitTableCell` on an unmerged cell — where `doc.splitCell` changes nothing — still drops the image selection and pushes a `docStore.snapshot()`. The test 'a table op called outside a table leaves it alone' only covers the `!cellInfo` case, so this narrower no-op path is unasserted. Impact is contained (the user just loses the selection), but it contradicts the stated rule that a call which mutates nothing leaves the selection alone.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. undoFn (editor.ts:2104) and redoFn (2139) clear `selectedImage` but leave `imageResizeDrag` live, unlike resetAfterDocumentReplace (3913-3914) and dispose (3931-3932) which clear both. The drag snapshots its own blockId/offset at 2603-2612 and installs document-level listeners (2614-2615), so it survives the undo. Keyboard reachability mid-drag is real: the image selection focuses the hidden textarea (2258), TextEditor.handleKeyDown calls imageKeyHandler first (text-editor.ts:865), Cmd+Z falls to the catch-all at editor.ts:2442 (nulls selectedImage, returns false), and text-editor.ts:1090-1098 then invokes the wired undoFn (2263). Afterwards render() still takes the `if (imageResizeDrag)` branch (1845) painting a preview for a non-existent selection, and handleImageResizeMouseUp (2515-2559) commits doc.applyInlineStyle at the stale (blockId, offset) (2550-2556); its only guards are doc.getBlock and findImageAtOffset (2538-2543), which pass precisely when a different image occupied that offset after the undo — a silent wrong-target document write. No other clear site exists (all imageResizeDrag references: 1302, 1845-1860, 2491-2524, 2603, 2788, 3914, 3932), and handleImageHover's `if (imageResizeDrag) return true` (2788) does not clear it. Stale state surviving an invalidating operation causing a wrong document mutation is in the correctness lane and blocking.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. editor.ts:2538 calls `doc.getBlock(blockId)` and then tests `block ? ... : null` at 2539; `Doc.getBlock` (document.ts:174-188) throws at line 187 when the block is absent, so the ternary and the `if (!current)` fallback (2540) are dead for the missing-block case and the throw escapes the document-level `mouseup` listener registered at editor.ts:2615. The sibling image paths were hardened to `doc.findBlock` with explicit comments about this exact throw hazard (editor.ts:2313-2314, 2332-2337, 3799, 3812, 3826), so no invariant guarantees the block exists here. I searched for a guard that would make it unreachable and found none: `imageResizeDrag` is never cleared on undo or on a remote change (only assignments/clears are 2603, 2524, 3914, 3932), and `undoFn` (2096-2134) clears `selectedImage` at 2104 but leaves `imageResizeDrag` intact while `docStore.undo()`/`doc.refresh()` can remove the block; collaborative editing (Yorkie presence at 2112, peer-cursor.ts) makes remote deletion during a long drag reachable. In-lane (missing-guard crash / dead guard on a stale coordinate read), and the cost when it fires is an uncaught exception out of a global listener with the resize silently dropped.
